+import re
+
+import pytest
+
+from lark import TextSlice
+from lark.common import LexerConf
+from lark.lexer import BasicLexer, PatternRE, PatternStr, Scanner, TerminalDef, Token
+
+
+class GroupLimitedRE:
+    error = re.error
+
+    def __init__(self, limit):
+        self.limit = limit
+
+    def compile(self, pattern, flags=0):
+        compiled = re.compile(pattern, flags)
+        if not compiled.groupindex:
+            raise RuntimeError("attempted an empty scanner batch")
+        if len(compiled.groupindex) > self.limit:
+            raise AssertionError("named group limit exceeded")
+        return compiled
+
+    def match(self, pattern, text, flags=0):
+        return re.match(pattern, text, flags)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_bytes", [False, True])
+def test_split_preserves_prefix_and_first_match(use_bytes):
+    terminals = [
+        TerminalDef("A", PatternRE("a+")),
+        TerminalDef("B", PatternStr("b")),
+        TerminalDef("C", PatternRE(r"(?P<INNER>a+|c)")),
+        TerminalDef("D", PatternStr("d")),
+    ]
+    scanner = Scanner(terminals, re.I, GroupLimitedRE(2), use_bytes)
+
+    def text(value):
+        return value.encode("ascii") if use_bytes else value
+
+    assert scanner.match(TextSlice(text("!AAX"), 1, 3), 1) == (text("AA"), "A")
+    assert scanner.fullmatch(text("AA")) == "A"
+    for value, name in [("a", "A"), ("b", "B"), ("c", "C"), ("d", "D")]:
+        assert scanner.match(TextSlice.cast_from(text(value)), 0) == (text(value), name)
+        assert scanner.fullmatch(text(value)) == name
+    assert scanner.match(TextSlice.cast_from(text("q")), 0) is None
+    assert scanner.fullmatch(text("q")) is None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_prefix", [False, True])
+def test_unsplittable_terminal_propagates_assertion(with_prefix):
+    terminals = []
+    if with_prefix:
+        terminals.extend([
+            TerminalDef("A", PatternStr("a")),
+            TerminalDef("B", PatternStr("b")),
+        ])
+    terminals.append(TerminalDef("BAD", PatternRE(r"(?P<I>x)(?P<J>y)")))
+    with pytest.raises(AssertionError, match="named group limit"):
+        Scanner(terminals, 0, GroupLimitedRE(2), False)
+
+
+def test_embedded_literal_scanner_splits_and_retags():
+    terminals = [
+        TerminalDef("WORD", PatternRE("[a-z]+")),
+        TerminalDef("K1", PatternStr("if")),
+        TerminalDef("K2", PatternStr("in")),
+        TerminalDef("K3", PatternStr("int")),
+        TerminalDef("K4", PatternStr("else")),
+        TerminalDef("K5", PatternStr("end")),
+    ]
+    lexer = BasicLexer(LexerConf(terminals, GroupLimitedRE(2), skip_validation=True))
+    scanner = lexer.scanner
+    assert scanner.allowed_types == {"WORD"}
+    for literal, name in [("if", "K1"), ("in", "K2"), ("int", "K3"), ("else", "K4"), ("end", "K5")]:
+        matched = scanner.match(TextSlice.cast_from(literal), 0)
+        assert matched == (literal, "WORD")
+        token = Token("WORD", literal, 4, 2, 3, 2, 3 + len(literal), 4 + len(literal))
+        result = lexer.callback["WORD"](token)
+        assert result is token
+        assert result.type == name
+        assert result.value == literal
+        assert (result.start_pos, result.line, result.column, result.end_line, result.end_column, result.end_pos) == (4, 2, 3, 2, 3 + len(literal), 4 + len(literal))
+    token = Token("WORD", "identifier")
+    assert lexer.callback["WORD"](token) is token
+    assert token.type == "WORD"
spec.notes: This task targets a defect already present in the supplied snapshot, so it uses new hidden acceptance tests rather than introducing a synthetic setup regression. The controlled regex wrapper delegates compilation to re and rejects patterns exceeding a named-group limit. Its empty-pattern guard makes the current zero-sized fallback fail promptly instead of hanging. The successful-splitting case deliberately makes a later batch exceed the limit after an earlier batch has compiled, exposing loss of the compiled prefix. The singleton cases expose nontermination; the embedded-literal case supplies integration coverage. A correct repair must retain compiled prefixes and re-raise an unsplittable singleton's AssertionError, which is substantively different from the original callback-dispatch change.
spec.question: Harden `Scanner` against regex engines that raise `AssertionError` when a compiled pattern contains too many named groups. Oversized terminal batches should be split until they compile, without losing terminals or changing their order. Both `Scanner.match` and `Scanner.fullmatch` must continue choosing the first successful compiled batch, including when only a later batch requires further splitting. If a single terminal still cannot compile, propagate its `AssertionError`; do not retry with an empty batch or recurse indefinitely. The same fallback must work for the internal scanners used by `UnlessCallback` to recognize embedded literals, preserving their retagging behavior and token data. Support both string and byte patterns and retain the supplied regex flags. Return a unified diff against production files only, leaving tests unchanged.
